output.brief: The rejects come from the combination of Arnholt resin and Press 5's degraded dryer (D5). Neither alone causes them. On Press 5, Arnholt lots reject at about 10%, against 0.9% for Quillan. Arnholt on Press 7, which has a healthy dryer, rejects at 0.8%. The new operators are not the cause: second shift runs only on Press 5, and every operator group rejects about 10% on Arnholt and 0.9% on Quillan. Arnholt arrives wetter, at 0.27–0.33% moisture against 0.11–0.14% for Quillan. D5 can't dry it below the 0.20% limit. In a week-42 test, the same Arnholt lot dried in a good dryer gave 0.8% rejects, against 10.4% through D5. The Arnholt trial ran only on Press 7, so it could never have exposed this. Quillan alone was tolerable on D5. I'm quite confident in this. One caveat: all Arnholt resin was stored in the north annex, so I can't separate Arnholt's own wetness from the storage effect. Do not discipline the operators and do not drop Arnholt. This week, repair D5 (heater and desiccant), restore the original alarm limit, and keep Arnholt off D5 until its dew point is verified at −40 °C. Add a moisture check at the press feed throat for every resin lot. Test conditioned storage for Arnholt separately before spending on warehouse space.
